title: How tax revenue is spent
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:14Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T16:19:51Z autoreview: cleared with the fix (b wording)

match.reason: No bank point teaches the breakdown of where government spending goes; the closest card, Why governments collect tax, only mentions in general terms that tax pays for services and support payments, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: How tax revenue is spent
card: The government collects tax and then spends it. It spends on services and support that people share.
The biggest areas of spending are social security and welfare, health, education and defence.
payments and support for people who need help, such as the age pension or help for people who are looking for work.
roads, bridges, railways and other large structures that many people use. Government spending on infrastructure sits alongside the four big areas.
draft.remember: Tax revenue is spent on shared needs: welfare, health, education, defence and infrastructure.

a.q: Which of these is an example of government spending on infrastructure?
opts: Building a new bridge over a river
Paying the age pension to retirees
Paying doctors in a public hospital
Buying equipment for the armed forces
a.why: A bridge is a large structure that many people use, so it is infrastructure. The age pension is social security and welfare, which is a different area of spending.
a.clue: Infrastructure is built and used by many people.

b.q: Sam's family receives a payment from the government because a parent has lost their job and is looking for work. Which area of government spending does this belong to?
opts: Social security and welfare
Defence
Education
Infrastructure
b.why: Payments that support people who need help, such as people looking for work, are social security and welfare. Education is also a big area of spending, but it pays for schools and learning, not income support for families.
b.clue: The payment helps a person who needs support.

a.best: Building a new bridge over a river

problems.detail: The right option, 'Social security and welfare', is clearly the longest (four words against single-word distractors), so a student could pick it by length alone. A multi-word distractor such as 'Roads and other infrastructure' would balance it.

check.summary: The facts and both answers are correct. The only problem is that in question b the right option is much longer than the one-word distractors, so it stands out.
